title: Characteristic subgroups of $F_2$ with quotient $\mathrm{PSL}_{\binom{n}{2}}(\mathbb{F}_q)$ of arbitrarily large Lie rank
author: Liam Hanany
work: The Yang-Baxter Equation and Characteristic Finite Simple Quotients of the Free Group of Rank 2
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: original Theorem 1.2 of the article (source label Large rank quotients, source0.tex lines 65--68), the existence, for every $n\geq 3$, of infinitely many prime powers $q$ with a characteristic subgroup $C\leq F_2$ such that $F_2/C\simeq\mathrm{PSL}_{\binom{n}{2}}(\mathbb{F}_q)$, delivered with the author's own complete 15-line proof at source0.tex lines 974--988. H2: the proof is a chain of research-level inputs that the solver must assemble rather than a qualifying examination exercise. It must pass from the Zariski density of the $B_4$-representation on the Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov space to the Zariski density of the image of the normal subgroup $F_2$, extract from the eigenvalues of $\sigma_1\sigma_3^{-1}$ a quotient $\pm q^as^b\neq\pm 1$ that is not a root of unity, specialize the finitely generated integral domain $\mathbb{Q}[q^{\pm1},s^{\pm1}]$ at a closed point where the image is Zariski dense, identify the Zariski closure with $\mathrm{SL}_N$ through the projection to $\mathrm{PGL}_N$, invoke the Strong Approximation Theorem to obtain surjections onto $\mathrm{PSL}_N(\mathbb{F}_p)$ for infinitely many primes, and finally use the extension of the representation to $\mathrm{Aut}(F_2)$ to show that the kernel is characteristic. That synthesis, and in particular the passage from a Zariski-dense representation to characteristic finite simple quotients, is well beyond ordinary PhD qualifying level.
